reading: The input has one full coloured column on the left. Draw a 2 anti-diagonal from the top-right corner down to the cell just above the bottom-left of the free area, and fill the bottom row right of the column with 4.

slots.anchor: the full left column (any colour, kept)

why: on every pair the output is the input plus that anti-diagonal of 2 and bottom row of 4

reading: Among the bg-coloured (0) block shapes with a two-cell tail, the one sharing rows with the colour-5 staircase loses its tail, and its body side facing the staircase turns 6.
verb: retract tail and mark facing side

slots.subject: the 0 shape (body rectangle + 2-cell tail) whose rows overlap the colour-5 triangle
slots.marked: the body's edge column/row on the side toward the 5 triangle becomes 6

why: in both pairs exactly one 0 shape changes: tail erased, near-side edge of body recoloured 6; other shapes unchanged

reading: Four same-coloured corner cells mark a box; the shape inside takes the corner colour and the box interior (without the corners' rows/columns) is cut out.

new_rows.name: inside
new_rows.datalog:
miny(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxy(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
minx(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
inside(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), miny(A), maxy(B), minx(L), maxx(R), Y > A, Y < B, X > L, X < R.

why: output = strict interior of the bounding box of all fg (the 4 corners), with every inner fg cell in the corner colour

reading: Around each 3 cell stamp a fixed 5x5 pattern (5 roof, 2 walls, 8 floor) centred on it, then extend the floor line with 2 to both grid borders.

slots.extend source: the 8 floor segment, extended left and right in colour 2

why: each 3 gets the same 5x5 pattern centred on it, and the row two below each 3 is 2 everywhere outside the 8 floor

reading: Two vertical 5 columns capped by 8 at top and bottom bound a rectangle; cut out that rectangle (caps included).

new_rows.name: pillars
new_rows.datalog:
pillars(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 5.
pillars(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 8, Y2 = Y + 1, cell(Y2, X, D), D = 5.
pillars(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C), C = 8, Y2 = Y - 1, cell(Y2, X, D), D = 5.

why: output = bounding box of all 5 cells plus the 8 cells directly above/below them

reading: Single cells scattered beside a solid 5 band turn 5 and slide straight toward the band until they touch it (or the cells already stacked against it).

new_rows.name: dot
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
dot(Y, X) :- obj(O, Y, X), osize(O, N), N = 1.

why: every single cell becomes 5 and ends in contact with the band along its row/column, piling up in order; the band is unchanged
invariants: number of moved cells per row/column side preserved

reading: Draw a 3x3 ring of 1 around every isolated 5 cell.
why: every 5 marker is the centre of a 1 ring; nothing else changes

reading: The grid holds 5x5 framed panels; each empty panel is filled with the inner pattern of a panel of the same colour that has one.
verb: copy pattern to same-colour empty frames

slots.panels: 5x5 outlines laid out on a 6-cell lattice
slots.source: the same-colour panel whose 3x3 interior is non-empty
slots.paint: source interior pattern in the panel colour

why: every empty panel whose colour also appears on a patterned panel receives that pattern; others unchanged
invariants: empty panels with no same-colour donor stay empty

reading: Each cup of 1 (open slot on top) holds one coloured cell; fill the cup's inside, its slot, and the row just above the cup with that colour.

new_rows.name: cupfill
new_rows.datalog:
osize(O, count(Y, X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
cup(O) :- osize(O, N), N > 1.
top(O, min(Y)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
bot(O, max(Y)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
lef(O, min(X)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
rig(O, max(X)) :- cup(O), obj(O, Y, X).
inbox(O, Y, X) :- top(O, T), bot(O, B), lef(O, L), rig(O, R), px(Y, X, C), Y >= T, Y <= B, X >= L, X <= R.
cupfill(Y, X) :- inbox(O, Y, X), !obj(O, Y, X).
cupfill(Y, X) :- top(O, T), lef(O, L), rig(O, R), Y = T - 1, px(Y, X, C), X >= L, X <= R.

why: per cup: all non-cup cells of its bounding box plus the row above it take the colour of the single cell inside

reading: A dashed rectangle of 1 (sometimes with one dashed middle line) has its gaps filled with 2.

new_rows.name: gaps
new_rows.datalog:
isfg(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, C).
miny(min(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxy(max(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
minx(min(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
maxx(max(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
rowc(Y, count(X)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
colc(X, count(Y)) :- cell(Y, X, C).
lrow(Y) :- rowc(Y, N), N > 3.
lcol(X) :- colc(X, N), N > 3.
gaps(Y, X) :- lrow(Y), px(Y, X, C), !isfg(Y, X), minx(L), maxx(R), X >= L, X <= R.
gaps(Y, X) :- lcol(X), px(Y, X, C), !isfg(Y, X), miny(T), maxy(B), Y >= T, Y <= B.

why: every background cell on a row/column holding 4+ cells of 1, within the bounding box of the 1s, becomes 2; nothing else changes
